conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have children. I have three kids actually - Alex who's 10, Blake who's 19, and Charlie who's 2 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children - Alex (10), Blake (19), and Charlie (2).

Now I need to ask some questions about each child to assess eligibility. Let me start with Blake, who is 19.

Is Blake currently in approved education or training? For example, is Blake enrolled in full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels or equivalent) or an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and hasn't been studying since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that about Blake.

Now, let me ask about your living situation. Do all three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) live with you in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I live in the UK - in Manchester actually. Alex and Blake both live at home with me, but Charlie doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

Regarding Charlie who lives with his mum - do you contribute toward Charlie's upbringing? For example, do you pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount for Charlie's care, or provide regular financial support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not really contributing financially at the moment. I'm not able to help out with money for Charlie right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Now, regarding Alex and Blake who live with you - are you responsible for them? In other words, are you their parent or guardian, and do you provide for their care and upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm their parent and I look after them both - I provide for everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment. Are Alex, Blake, and Charlie all usually resident in the UK? (Even though Charlie lives with his mum, is he still living in the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, all three of them are in the UK. Charlie lives with his mum here in the UK as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

Are you or any of the children subject to immigration control, or are there any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there aren't any immigration restrictions or anything like that. We all have the right to be here.

Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, here's my assessment of your Child Benefit eligibility:

**Alex (age 10): ELIGIBLE ✓**
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alex is under 16, lives with you, and you're their parent who is responsible for their care.

**Blake (age 19): INELIGIBLE ✗**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Blake. While Blake lives with you, Child Benefit only continues for young people aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training. Since Blake isn't currently in any education or training, you cannot claim Child Benefit for them.

**Charlie (age 2): INELIGIBLE ✗**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Charlie. Although Charlie is under 16, they don't live with you, and you're not contributing financially to their care. To claim Child Benefit for a child who doesn't live with you, you would need to contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount toward their upbringing.

**Summary:** You can claim Child Benefit for Alex only. If Blake returns to full-time non-advanced education or approved training in the future, you may become eligible to claim for them again until they turn 20 (or until they finish their course if that's earlier).
